name: getitimer
synopsis: int setitimer(int which, const struct itimerval *restrict new_value, struct itimerval *_Nullable restrict old_value);
description: getitimer retrieves the current value of a specified interval timer and stores it in the provided buffer. Interval timers count down against different clocks and generate signals upon expiration.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Specifies the type of timer: ITIMER_REAL, ITIMER_VIRTUAL, or ITIMER_PROF

parameters.name: curr_value
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure where the current timer value is stored

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: curr_value is not a valid pointer
which is not one of ITIMER_REAL, ITIMER_VIRTUAL, or ITIMER_PROF

bugs: Under heavy loading, an ITIMER_REAL timer may expire before the previous signal is delivered, potentially losing the signal. Before Linux 2.6.16, timer values exceeding MAX_SEC_IN_JIFFIES were silently truncated.
